name: Kansas
source: Kansas reader session (Stage 5 tools), 2026-11-18: the November 2026 Open States dump converted with scripts/stage5/openstates/; every floor roll call of a 146-bill dry batch (55 roll calls, 4,920 member votes) read from www.kslegislature.gov with the verifier's own fetch, and each member's vote compared with the dump. Three bill texts were read for their marks (2021 HB 2058 as introduced and as amended, 2025 HB 2052 as introduced); no text was measured in bulk.
sessions: One two-year session (a biennium: 2017-2018, 2019-2020, ... 2025-2026), meeting from the second Monday of January to April or May each year. Bill numbers run through the whole biennium and do not start again in the second year: House bills HB 2001 up, Senate bills SB 1 up, House concurrent resolutions HCR 5001 up, House resolutions HR 6001 up, Senate concurrent resolutions SCR 1601 up, Senate resolutions SR 1701 up. A bill passed in a changed form keeps its number with a prefix ("Sub for HB 2278", "H Sub for SB 116"). A special session is its own session with its own numbers (2020S1: June 2020; 2021S1: November 2021); the site names them b2020s and b2021s. The site names a biennium b2025_26. House 125 seats, Senate 40.
bill_data: No LegiScan dataset is on disk for Kansas. Bills, sponsors and roll calls come from Open States data, converted to the same folder layout (KS-900097 to KS-900103: the five bienniums 2017-2018 to 2025-2026 and the 2020 and 2021 special sessions; scripts/stage5/openstates/README.md). Each folder carries a .openstates.json; its ids are ours and no legiscan.com page exists for them.

The dump holds far fewer roll calls for 2019-2020 (376) and 2023-2024 (614) than for the bienniums either side (about 1,050 to 1,430), and its vote addresses are the old host's, www.kslegislature.org/li/..., which now redirect to a 404. So no Kansas dump vote is placed: scripts/stage5/openstates/fetch-legislature-rollcalls.ts reads each bill's vote list from the legislature (the archive's bill page for 2017-2022 and the specials, the bill's history page filtered to votes for 2023 on), keeps the votes on the bill and reads each from its own page; convert.py places only those (record_is_the_floor) and keeps every other dump vote marked committee, with the reason in _openstates.not_placed. Run the fetch for every bill the scan finds, then convert the whole state again.

Compared 2026-11-18, 2017-2026: 55 floor roll calls read from the record, 0 refused. All 55 have a dump copy (the 11 of 2023-2024 matched by bill, chamber and day, since that biennium's dump addresses lead nowhere). Tally differences: 0. Member votes compared: 4,920, differences: 0 (200 matched in a second pass that compares the dump's split labels, such as "A." and "Smith", as lists). Two members changed their names: Tory Arnberger is printed "Blew" from 2023 (Tory Marie Blew), and Stephanie Clayton is Stephanie Sawyer-Clayton. 38 dump votes on the scanned bills were not read: Committee of the Whole votes and motions.

The record prints no given name, so the reader builds each member's full name from the legislature's member id (rep_<surname>_<given>_<n>) and the surname the page prints; convert.py links a record name to an Open States person by family name and a fitting given name (ms_full_names). Roster legislators: 165, all linked; 9 by the legislature's member id or district rather than by name (Woodard, Goddard, Joseph Claeys, Lisa M. Moser, Fagg, Murphy, Mike Thompson in the Senate, Ryckman, Clifford). Three are by hand, in name_overrides.json: Michael Murphy in the House 2021-2024 (now a senator), Brandon Woodard in the House 2023-2024, and Joseph Claeys in the Senate 2025-2026. Dan Goddard (House District 7, 2023-2026) is missing from the legislature's member list page; his own page is there. All 4,920 placed record votes link to a person.

Open States names and the record's names can differ by a given-name form (record 'Charles Smith', rep_smith_charles_1, is the Open States person Chuck Smith; 'William Sutton', rep_sutton_william_1, is Bill Sutton). The converter then files the record's votes under a second, record-only person id with no idmap line. link_check does not see this (the Open States person is linked); the pre-fill's list of people with no vote does. Fix by an idmap line from the record-only id to the person, then patch the person id in the skeletons and store copies (seen 2026-11-18, gun-policy set-up).

votes.floor_rule: A vote is cited on its own page. 2017-2022 and the special sessions are an archive: www.kslegislature.gov/<li_YYYY>/<biennium>/measures/vote_view/je_<stamp>/ (li_2018/b2017_18, li_2020/b2019_20, li_2022/b2021_22, li_2020s/b2020s, li_2021s/b2021s; /li_2018/b2017_18/measures/vote_view/je_20180215112754_700284/). 2023 on is the current site: /<biennium>/vote/?apn=<biennium>/year<1|2>/<house|senate>/legislative_days/day<NNN>_<YYYYMMDD>/vote_records/<file>.odt (an HTML page despite the .odt). The page prints the chamber, the question ("Final Action - Passed as amended;"), the day, the bill, the tally (Yea, Nay, Present but not Voting or Present and Passing, Absent and Not Voting, Not Voting) and each member as a link to the member's page in that session, with the surname only ("Alcala", "B. Carpenter", "Carpenter, W." when two share one). So the reader (src/lib/stateRollCallEvidence.ts) builds the full name from the member id in the link: the given words that follow the printed surname, then the surname (rep_carpenter_blake_1 -> Blake Carpenter; rep_paige_wanda_1 -> Wanda Brownlee Paige). A vote is read only when its question is a vote on the bill (final action and emergency final action, a conference committee report, concurring in the other chamber's amendments, a veto override, the consent calendar), each group lists the count its heading prints (and on the current site the count both tallies print), the total is not more than the chamber's seats, and the page's chamber, day and session are the address's. Concurring is counted as a vote on the bill: Kansas sends the bill on after it and no other vote follows. A member who did not vote is written as the page lists them (Present, Absent, Not voting), never as a Yea or a Nay. Committee of the Whole votes (amendments, motions, its own recommendation) are not mapped.
gaps: A Committee of the Whole vote (on an amendment, a motion, or the committee's recommendation) and every other motion is not a vote on the bill and is not mapped (runner, 2026-11-16).

A member whose id does not open with a surname word the page prints, or leaves no given word, or whose printed initial is not the given name's, is kept as printed and gives no line. In the dry batch none did after two fixes: a member under a later family name is rendered with the printed name (rep_arnberger_tory_1 printed "Blew" is Tory Blew; rep_leehahn_tatum_1 printed "Lee" is Tatum Lee), and the reader reads an initial after the surname ("Carpenter, W.").

The 2023-2024 dump rows carry the old je_ vote address, which leads nowhere on either host: that biennium's votes come only from the fetch. The special sessions held no bill in the scan, so their reading is proved on one 2020S1 page only.

texts.marks: Measured on 3 texts (2021 HB 2058 as introduced and as amended by the House Committee of the Whole, 2025 HB 2052 as introduced; 2026-11-18). A bill as introduced prints words added to existing law in italics and words deleted from existing law struck through with a drawn line; a wholly new section is in italics. An amended version keeps those marks and adds its own: words a committee added are in italics, and words the Committee of the Whole added are in bold inside {braces}; words an amendment removed are struck through. The version's name is printed at the top ("As Amended by House Committee", "{As Amended by House Committee of the Whole}"). Plain pdftotext loses all three: italics and bold print as plain text, and a struck word runs into its replacement with no mark ("(e)(f)" where (e) is struck). pdftohtml -xml shows italics as <i> and bold as <b>, but not the drawn strike line; read with a PDF library that sees drawn lines, or look at the page as an image, before quoting a passage near a change. Confirmed on 26 texts (2026-11-18, PyMuPDF): italics and the drawn strike line both read; the enacting clause ('Be it enacted ...') prints in italics, so it reads as added words and is not a change.
texts.note: The dump links each text as an old-host PDF; convert.py rewrites them (ks_texts). 2017-2022 and the specials: /<li_YYYY>/<biennium>/measures/documents/<bill>_<NN>_0000.pdf (hb2058_00_0000.pdf as introduced, _02_ and up amended, also <bill>_enrolled.pdf). 2023 on: /<biennium>/bills/download/?apn=<biennium>/year<1|2>/ready_for_publication/<hb_2052>/<hb2052_00_0000>.pdf; the apn's year is not checked (year1 and year2 serve the same file). A bill's page is /<li_YYYY>/<biennium>/measures/<hb2476>/ (lower case) in the archive and /<biennium>/bills/<SB113>/ or /<biennium>/resolutions/<HCR5020>/ on the current site.

search_note: Kansas sponsorships and House and Senate floor votes for 2017 to 2026 come from the bill data on disk, checked against the legislature's own record: skip the legislature's bill pages and vote pages, and add the place "sponsor list: covered by bulk bill data". Spend the search on their own words (statements, campaign pages, newsletters, floor remarks, interviews, questionnaires). If any page returns 403, 429, an empty page or a bot check, record it as blocked and move on: do not retry it with a different user agent, headers or tool.
bill_table_note:
- Kansas sessions run two years (a biennium); bill numbers do not start again in the second year.
- Floor votes kept: final action (and emergency final action), conference committee reports, concurring in the other chamber's amendments, veto overrides and the consent calendar. Committee of the Whole votes, amendments and motions are not floor votes on the bill.
- A bill passed as a substitute keeps its number ("Sub for HB 2278"); a vote on the substitute is a vote on the bill.
- Texts: italics = added to existing law (or added by a committee in an amended version), {bold in braces} = added by the Committee of the Whole, struck-through words = deleted. Plain text loses all three marks.
quirks: The site has no robots.txt (404) and states no crawl delay. The reader waits one second between requests. No 403, 429 or bot check was met on 2026-11-18.
The old host, www.kslegislature.org/li/..., redirects to a 404 for every vote, bill and text address in the dump; convert.py rewrites them to www.kslegislature.gov.
Archive bill pages need a lower-case bill in the path (/measures/hb2476/); the current site needs upper case and files resolutions apart from bills (/resolutions/HCR5020/; /bills/HCR5020/ is a 404).
A bill's history page with no recorded vote prints "No votes recorded yet." and no table; the fetch reads that as no votes only when the page shows no vote rows and no vote link.
A bill passed as a substitute is titled "Sub for HB 2278" or "S Sub for HB 2089" on its vote list; the fetch accepts the prefix.

One vote is one page and needs nothing else. The line tool took 49 seconds for 200 random votes from an empty page cache (48 roll calls), and 58 seconds for all 3,552 vote pairs of the dry batch from an empty cache.
The Senate heads one group "Present and Passing" where the House says "Present but not Voting"; both are read as Present.

Several bills are gut-and-amend substitutes: a bill's early floor vote can be on an unrelated text (2023 HB 2056 as introduced was an elections bill; 2023 SB 116 as introduced was school safety lessons, later a licence-fee bill). Read each vote on the version it was taken on; the bill's history page names the version.
